extracted.intended_audience: authors preparing manuscripts for American Meteorological Society (AMS) journals
extracted.subtask_description: Guidelines for formatting mathematical expressions, variable/typeface conventions, operators, units, time, and date when preparing manuscripts for AMS publications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Display versus in-line equations
rubrics_metrics.description: Display equations are centered on their own line and are usually numbered but do not have to be. In-line equations appear in running text.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When citing display equations in text, use either Eq. ( ) or ( ) consistently; do not mix the two styles.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of MathType in Microsoft Word
rubrics_metrics.description: When using Microsoft Word to prepare a manuscript, use MathType for display equations and other complicated mathematical expressions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Equation numbers should be given outside of MathType and surrounded by parentheses, such as (1). In-line equations and uncomplicated expressions may be entered using MathType or typed directly from the keyboard.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inline equation structure and fencing (no stacking)
rubrics_metrics.description: In-line equations should not be built up or stacked; instead, use fencing to make clear the order of calculation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The AMS fencing hierarchy is {[( )]}: for instance, (a+10){[b+(c+5)]/(d−12)}. Deviations are allowed only if the usage is defined (e.g., 'square brackets indicate a time mean'). The sequence may be repeated if more than three levels of fencing are needed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consistent variable style and Times New Roman
rubrics_metrics.description: Use AMS style for variables consistently in text, equations, figures, and tables. They should be set as Times New Roman, although some exceptions apply such as script letters and matrix characters.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Apply the typeface rules below uniformly across the manuscript.

rubrics_metrics.name: Single-character scalar variables, indices, constants: italic
rubrics_metrics.description: Single-character scalar variable, index, constant, or abbreviation should be set in italic.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: t, u, w, x, y, z, υ, θ, i, j, C_D, T_a. Note: Greek upsilon is used for the lowercase italic vee (v) to avoid confusion with the Greek letter nu (ν).

rubrics_metrics.name: Multiple-character scalars, nondimensional numbers, and acronyms: nonitalic
rubrics_metrics.description: Multiple-character scalar variable, abbreviation, nondimensional number, or acronym should be set in regular (nonitalic) type.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: Re, Ro, abs, max, min, Re, Im.

rubrics_metrics.name: Vectors (Roman letters): boldface nonitalic; arrows replaced by bold
rubrics_metrics.description: Vectors in Roman letters should be set in boldface nonitalic.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: V, v, x, i, j, k. Boldface type replaces an arrow above a vector.

rubrics_metrics.name: Matrices (Roman letters): boldface Arial or Helvetica
rubrics_metrics.description: Matrices in Roman letters should be set in boldface Arial or Helvetica.

rubrics_metrics.name: Vector and matrix Greek letters: boldface; italic/nonitalic by case
rubrics_metrics.description: Vector and matrix Greek letters should be boldface. Use italic if lowercase and nonitalic if uppercase.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: λ, τ, Γ, Ω set boldface; follow the lowercase/uppercase italicization rule.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mathematical operators and special notation typeface
rubrics_metrics.description: Operators and common function names should be set in regular (nonitalic) type.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: sin, cos, arctan, tanh, sgn, const, c.c. The 'order of' notation O( ) is set italic: O( ). Units are placed outside the parentheses. For complicated arguments to exponential functions, use exp( ) instead of e( ).

rubrics_metrics.name: Use SI units with a few approved non-SI exceptions
rubrics_metrics.description: Units should be SI with the exception of several approved non-SI units (e.g., cfs, mb).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow AMS-approved non-SI allowances when necessary.

rubrics_metrics.name: Unit abbreviations, font, spacing, and negative exponents
rubrics_metrics.description: Use unit abbreviations only when preceded by a numeral. Set units in Times New Roman font with spaces between components of compound units. Use negative signs for denominators.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example formatting: 5 meters per second should be set as 5 m s−1.

rubrics_metrics.name: Hyphenation of number–unit pairs when used as modifiers
rubrics_metrics.description: Number–unit pairs should be hyphenated when they modify a noun, and not hyphenated when not used as modifiers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Modifier examples: '10-km length; 5-day intervals'. Non-modifier examples: 'the trench is 75 m deep; a height of 12 m.'

rubrics_metrics.name: Time annotation: UTC preferred and 24-hour clock required
rubrics_metrics.description: The recommended time annotation is coordinated universal time (UTC). Please use UTC instead of Z or GMT.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Other time zones are permitted if they are defined. Four-digit astronomical or military time (24-hour clock) is required. Example: '1500 UTC 3 May 2015' for May 3, 2015 at 3:00 p.m. GMT.

rubrics_metrics.name: Date format: Day Month Year; month abbreviations limited
rubrics_metrics.description: Dates must be written in 'Day Month Year' format.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Abbreviations for months are permitted only in figures, tables, and their captions.
